by: hansard-1 session, ruling 96 (to be appended by the integrator)
title: Parliament's Hansard transcripts the old estate holds as text rows, with its roster and its derived speeches, as exported once from its tables

landmarks: one JSON object per line, its `kind` one of member, section, sitting, speech
section lines carry sitting_date, section_index, proceeding, subject, speakers, speech_count, url, body_hash and text

signals_note: Not a document Parliament published: an export of the rows the old estate captured from hansard.parliament.nz (incoming_news.hansard_sections and hansard_members) and derived from them (nzbn_canonical registers.hansard_sittings and registers.hansard_speeches), made once on 26 October 2026. Every row from it is 'taken from the old estate's tables; original not held'.
notes: 16,081 lines: 394 members, 3,923 sections of 137 sitting days (20 November 2024 to 23 September 2026), 137 sittings, 11,627 derived speech rows (75 retired by the old derive). 47,243 speech turns in the sections' speaker lists: 40,098 carry Parliament's member id, 7,145 only a role (the Speaker, the chair, the Clerk, unnamed interjections). body_hash is the SHA-1 of the section's text. The speaker labels are as the old capture read them from the page; the member id and name are its roster's. 262 sections have no text.
applies_to: every Hansard section the old estate captured, 20 November 2024 to 23 September 2026
process: One row per line by kind; one speech turn per speaker-list entry in its printed order; no model.
gates: Every line is read or set aside with a reason.
Each section's text hashes to its body_hash.
Each sitting's counts equal the sitting row's own (check.py).

title: A record of the query-nz ingest MCP's parliament-hansard-debates corpus: one sitting day's daily Hansard PDF as its provider read it with pdftotext -layout

landmarks: sitting_date equal to the day in the address
text, page_count, word_count, sha256 of the PDF, a capture block

signals_note: Captured and read off-estate by Arthur's provider (ruling 78; the estate's own capture may not pass parliament.nz's challenge, hard limit 6). The text is pdftotext -layout's, nothing derived; no section or speech split.
notes: 1,862 records on 27 October, 2003-02-11 to 2026-09-23, one per sitting day; 94,602,760 words, each record's word_count its text's whitespace words. A sitting under urgency that runs past midnight is one PDF per calendar day; the provider holds the first day's only (e.g. 2024-12-10 continued 11 to 13 December).
process: One days row per sitting day, from the version the pull saw last; the text to hansard_private.day_texts; each old section's subject looked for in the day's folded text; no model.
gates: Every document read, an older version, or set aside with a reason.
Words held equal to the MCP's measure within 1%.
Old subjects found in the day's text at or above the check's floor.

by: hansard-3 session (Fable), Arthur's common rules for the MCP names readers of 31 October 2026 (ruling 130 pending; to be appended by the integrator)
title: A sitting day of Parliament's Hansard as the MCP's debates record holds it: the daily PDF's text, pdftotext -layout, split into sections and speaker turns and read for the names in the speeches

landmarks: the mcp-hansard-debates-record shape: url https://hansard.parliament.nz/api/resources/daily/related/<day>/<day>-daily.pdf, sitting_date, text
final layout: body pages under a running head `20 Nov 2024   Oral Questions   7595` (or page number first), a cover and contents before, an index after
draft layout: `Subject to Revision—Not to be Quoted or Distributed` and `Page N   HOUSE OF REPRESENTATIVES   <date>` on every page

signals.measured_on: all 1,862 days held 31 October 2026: final 1,827 (2003-02-11 to 2026-04-23), draft 35 (2026-04-28 to 2026-09-23); 0 unrecognised
signals.speaker_lines_a_day: about 200 to 460; 1,300 to 3,200 on an urgency day

signals_note: Captured and read off-estate by the provider (ruling 78). The split is the estate's own, deterministic (registers/hansard/split.py, rule `hansard-day split 1`): headings are the centred lines (capitals from indent 1, mixed case centred within 10 of the page's middle), a section is the text under one run of heading lines, a turn is a paragraph opening `NAME (role or Party—Electorate) [(hh:mm)] [to the Minister …]:` in capitals, a role, or a mixed-case name seen in capitals that day or held by the old roster. Proved on the 137 days both sources hold (hansard-3): the split finds more member turns than the old speaker lists on 129 days (the old lists skip the question line and most debate speakers) and fewer on the 8 urgency sittings whose later calendar days the MCP lacks.
prompt:
You read one piece of a New Zealand parliamentary debate (Hansard): speeches by members, each opening with the speaker's name in capitals or a role such as SPEAKER, then what they said. Answer with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"summary": "<one sentence, at most 40 words, saying what this piece of the debate is about, naming nobody>",
 "names": [{"name": "<a person or body named in the speeches, exactly as printed>", "kind": "person" | "company" | "agency" | "body" | "other", "role": "<the role the text gives them, in the text's own words, e.g. Minister of Finance, chief executive, constituent, former member, the applicant; null when none>", "of": "<for a person: the organisation the text says they are of or from, as printed; otherwise null>"}]}
Rules. List every person, company, government agency or department, council, court, iwi, trust, union, charity and other body that a speaker NAMES in a speech, each once. Do not list the speakers themselves (the names that open a paragraph before a colon) unless another speaker names them in a speech. A company or incorporated business is kind company; a ministry, department, Crown entity, council, police or court is kind agency; any other organisation is kind body; a named individual is kind person; use other when the kind cannot be told. Keep spelling, initials and honorifics as printed; never expand an initial; never add an address, an age or any fact the text does not state; never name anyone the text does not name. A role or party alone ("the Minister", "National") is not a name.
notes: The reader's budget is 40,000 characters of speech a request: the text-reader profile's context is 16,384 tokens, the answer 4,096, the prompt about 420, and Hansard English measured at about 4.3 characters a token (31 October 2026). A day is read in pieces: one per section within the budget; a section over it cut at speaker turns, then paragraphs, then lines, each part within the budget; a piece's reading stored at page p under the day's hash, the pieces joined into one reading at page 1 (settings `joined`). The speakers are the turns' own rows and are not asked for.
applies_to: every record of parliament-hansard-debates, once recognised as mcp-hansard-debates-record
process: Recognise the layout by its page furniture; drop the furniture, the cover, contents and index.
Headings to sections, speaker lines to turns, the member matched to the old roster within the day's Parliament; the counts into `days`, the rows into `day_sections` and `day_turns` (no model).
The text reader over every piece within the budget; the readings joined under the day's hash; the load picks the names into `people` and `pub.hansard_people`; never a link, never a claim.
gates: Every day split or set aside at stage read with the reason (no pages, no body page).
Every piece within the budget, or the day set aside naming the piece.
One reading per piece and one joined reading per day hash; a reading under another profile version fails the check.
Every name row cites the day's record, piece and ordinal.
on_fail: set aside at read; the check fails
